memory_candidates.content: When a new bash script sources scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh (or any library ending in a `read -r -d '' VAR <<'HEREDOC'` heredoc assignment) under its own `set -e`, guard the `source`/`.` call with `if ! . "$file"; then ...; fi` rather than a bare `source`. The heredoc read always returns exit status 1 at EOF (no literal NUL byte present), and under `set -e` an unguarded source call aborts the whole script right there -- even though the library's own last top-level statement (e.g. a function definition) would otherwise make the source succeed. Running the source as an `if` condition suspends -e checking for its entire execution. Precedent: task-lock.sh and orchestrate-batch-admit.sh already use this guard around this same library.

A lint that resolves citations (backtick-delimited paths) against ONLY a repo's root will produce heavy false positives in this dual-tree (source-store / deployed `.claude/`) repo structure, because authored prose commonly cites a path relative to the deployed tree (`commands/orchestrate.md`) or relative to a source-store extension directory with the `agent-system/extensions/` prefix dropped but the extension name (`core/`, `lean/`) kept as the citation's own first segment. Resolve against a small ordered list of candidate roots (repo root; repo_root/.claude if present; repo_root/agent-system/extensions if present) rather than a single root, before reporting a citation as unresolved. Also skip any candidate containing whitespace (a shell command or prose list quoted in backticks, not a path) and any candidate using a literal `...` elision marker.
